You're encouraged to post your selfmade 3D images in this subverse.

To take 3D images, just take a picture with your camera, then move the camera slightly to the right (about 6cm/ 2.3in) and quickly take another image. This won't work well on things that move fast (e.g. trees when it's windy, the sea, cars, etc.). If you have two cameras available, hold them next to each other and simultaneously take pictures with both cameras.

Now you have two images, one that's taken for your left eye and one that's taken for your right eye. Create a new image with a width double the width of one of the original images (e.g. if one of your images has a width of 1080px, your new image should have a width of 1080px*2 = 2160px). Now put your left image on the left of this new image, and the right one next to the left one. If you can't manage to do it, just post both images here and I'll do it for you!

There's an android app which I am using (beware of the many ads).

If you want to test your 3D images, just post them here and we can discuss them. If you want to submit your 3D images to the Front Page, you might want to tag them with [OC].

Happy 3D'ing!

So after a burnt valve and thrown rod, the whole engine has been rebuilt complete with forged internals. Hopefully this weekend we will get it started up! What is your routine for an engine break in? My understanding is to take out the spark plugs and crank the engine a few times to get the oil turning, and then to replace the plugs and start it, keeping the RPMs between 1-2K for 20 minutes. Then drive it just down the street and change the oil. I have Royal Purple break in oil, which I plan on running for the first 500 miles. I have penzoil non-synthetic to start it with of course. Then you just gradually drive it more and more. Does this sound like a safe plan, or am I headed for disaster? How have you broken in an engine?
[2003.5 MazdaSpeed Protege] Engine break in questions

I have never done a rebuild myself, but the shop I work at goes by this:

  • Prime oil system
  • Break in oil
  • fan in front of radiator
  • RED coolant in the rad (Dexcool)
  • 2K rpm 20 minutes or so while monitoring all the parameters (we have and old phone we connect to the ECM to do this)
  • Cooldown and repeat before test drive

This all makes good sense to me for most motor. I have always heard 2hrs @ 2k rpm and then changing the oil again. (to be honest) The only knowledge I have with complete rebuilds however, is with older Chevrolet motors sans EFI and all fancy electronic add-ons.
